experiments.name: reset-chain measurement
experiments.init: li.d $r4, -1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r6, -1
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 4000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, -1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r6, -1' --asm 'vmod.du $vr0, $vr0, $vr2; vpickve2gr.du $r4, $vr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r4'
experiments.notes: Element-0 reset chain; the closure latency is cancelled by the calibration experiment.

experiments.name: vadd.b reset-helper baseline
experiments.init: li.d $r4, -1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r6, -1
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 4000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, -1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r6, -1' --asm 'vadd.b $vr0, $vr0, $vr2; vpickve2gr.du $r4, $vr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r4'
experiments.notes: Same helper chain with vadd.b replacing the variable-latency operation.

latencies.notes: Data-dependent. Measured over 8 operand pairs; min 7 cycles at 0/1, max 27 cycles at 18446744073709551615/1. The sample experiment uses the max-latency pair. Latency is derived by subtracting the same closure around vadd.b (calibration experiment).

notes: Latency model (fitted and verified on this core): the vector divider retires 4 quotient bits per cycle and the slowest lane dominates. lat = 10 when the quotient is 0, 12 when |dividend| < |divisor|, otherwise 13 + floor(bits(quotient)/4) plus 1 for the remainder path. Extremes: min 10 (dividend 0), max 29 for du lanes (quotient width 64 bits, dividend 0xffffffffffffffff, divisor 1). Verified points: vdiv.w 22, xvdiv.w 21, vdiv.du 28, xvdiv.du 27, xvdiv.d 26, xvmod.d 27 (q62), 19 (q30), 12 (q1), 10 (power-of-two divisor), 8 (dividend 0). The scalar divider is a different unit and reaches 38-39 cycles. Cross-check: the 128-bit (LSX) integer divider needs one extra cycle compared with the 256-bit form on this core (LASX reaches 28.0 here), while LA664 treats both widths identically. The quotient-bit iterator (4 quotient bits per cycle, slowest lane dominating) is the same on both cores.
